function trailRowToMetadata(row: TrailRow): TrailMetadata {
  const reviewers = Array.isArray(row.reviewers)
    ? (row.reviewers as unknown as TrailReviewer[])
    : []
  return {
    number: row.number,
    branch: row.branch ?? row.original_branch,
    base: row.base,
    title: row.title,
    status: row.status,
    type: row.type,
    author: row.author,
    assignees: row.assignees,
    created_at: row.created_at,
    updated_at: row.updated_at,
    merged_at: row.merged_at,
    priority: (row.priority ?? "none") as TrailPriority,
    reviewers,
    requested_reviewers: row.requested_reviewers ?? [],
    merge_base_sha: row.merge_base_sha,
    head_sha: row.head_sha,
  }
}

function trailRowToReviews(row: TrailRow): TrailReviews {
  const rev = row.reviews as unknown
  if (rev && typeof rev === "object" && "reviews" in (rev as Record<string, unknown>)) {
    return rev as TrailReviews
  }
  return { reviews: [] }
}

/**
 * Build a URL-safe, decorative title slug for a trail detail URL, Linear-style.
 *
 * The slug is informational only — the API and route both key on the
 * per-repo trail `number`. When the slug in the URL doesn't match the
 * current title slug, the detail page replaces the URL with the canonical
 * form so links shared from the browser stay readable.
 *
 * Returns `undefined` when the title is empty or contains only characters
 * that would slugify to nothing (emoji, CJK, all-symbol). Callers should
 * pass the result straight into a Link's `params` so an empty slug omits
 * the segment entirely (`/trails/42`) rather than emitting a stray
 * trailing slash (`/trails/42/`).
 *
 * Rules:
 * - lower-case
 * - NFD-normalize and strip combining marks so `café` → `cafe`
 * - non-alphanumeric collapsed to "-"
 * - runs of "-" collapsed to a single "-"
 * - leading/trailing "-" trimmed
 * - capped at ~60 characters (trimmed on a dash boundary when possible)
 */
export function slugify(title: string): string | undefined {
  const normalized = title
    .normalize("NFD")
    .replace(/\p{Diacritic}/gu, "")
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, "-")
    .replace(/-+/g, "-")
    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, "")

  if (normalized.length === 0) return undefined
  if (normalized.length <= 60) return normalized

  const truncated = normalized.slice(0, 60)
  const lastDash = truncated.lastIndexOf("-")
  // Prefer cutting on a dash boundary when the boundary is reasonably close to the end
  if (lastDash > 40) return truncated.slice(0, lastDash)
  return truncated.replace(/-+$/, "")
}

Done. Both `trail create` and `trail show` now surface the trail's web URL.

**Trail filed:** https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/640 (#640)

**What changed (the right way — backend returns the URL, CLI consumes it):**

- **Backend** (`~/src/entirehq/entire.io`, branch `feat/trail-web-url`): trail resource now carries a canonical `url` field built from `FRONTEND_BASE_URL`, populated at all 5 response sites (list/create/detail/update via one `trailWebUrl` helper). - **CLI** (this repo, branch `feat/trail-web-url`): `trail create` now prints a `URL:` line; both create and show prefer the server's `url`, falling back to local construction only for older servers. This is what avoids lockstep — when the route changes, the CLI just uses whatever the server returns.

**Why the live trail's URL was locally constructed:** prod hasn't deployed the backend change yet, so the response had no `url` and the CLI fallback kicked in. It's a valid working link; once the backend ships, the CLI uses the server's canonical URL verbatim.
